falsifier_statement: qmirror.ghz.run(3, 1024) returns M in [3.7, 4.0] over 30 trials AND M_min >= 3.5
substrate: Aer state-vector (3 qubits) + numpy_native fallback path
circuit: GHZ-3 = H_0 + CNOT_01 + CNOT_12 (then per-basis rotation: H for X, S^dag+H for Y)
wall_seconds_estimate: ~2 s for 30k shots on Mac (Aer SV)
raw9_disclosure: ghz_mermin_runner.py is the SECOND .py file under qmirror standalone modules (after aer_runner.py); hexa-strict module is ghz_mermin.hexa
raw15_compliance: no personal paths in artifact bodies; bridge resolved via NEXUS_QMIRROR_BRIDGE_PATH env or HOME-relative fallback
raw10_caveats: Noiseless Aer SV reproduces analytic M=4.0 exactly because GHZ is a perfect simultaneous +/-1 eigenstate of XXX/XYY/YXY/YYX; shot noise is zero on Pauli eigenstates. Real-hardware (IBM/IonQ/Rigetti) would exhibit finite-fidelity decay (M_observed in [3.0, 3.8] typical) requiring readout-correction + ZNE to clear the >=3.7 threshold.

Mermin-3 witness is a *necessary* but not *sufficient* genuine-3-partite-entanglement witness; M>=2 already certifies non-biseparability but does NOT distinguish GHZ from W-state mixtures at the witness-only granularity. A full GHZ-fidelity certificate requires state tomography (cond.9 process tomography in qmirror 2.0).

Convention choice: this run uses the task-spec sign convention M = <XXX> - <XYY> - <YXY> - <YYX> (analytic +4); the qmirror_2_axes_spec doc writes M = <XYY>+<YXY>+<YYX>-<XXX> (analytic -4). Same |M|=4; verdict band [3.7,4.0] is on signed M per task spec. Cross-doc readers must check sign convention before comparing.

$0 default substrate is Aer-only; no QPU shots submitted. Cross-tech reproduction (cond.7-style) is OUT OF SCOPE for cond.10 by design (qmirror_2_axes_spec §7 caveat #2). A future hardware-anchor sister cycle is the only path to elevate this to a hardware-witnessed claim.
